headline: A 2016 law created a temporary federal commission to plan activities honoring John F. Kennedy on the 100th anniversary of his birth.
what_it_does: The law creates the John F. Kennedy Centennial Commission. The commission plans and carries out activities to honor Kennedy's 100th birthday and advises federal, state, and local agencies and civic groups on similar events. It must report its revenue and spending to the President and Congress each year, and file a final report by August 31, 2017. The commission ends by September 30, 2017, and the Interior Department's Inspector General may audit it.
when_it_takes_effect: Enacted July 29, 2016; the commission was set to terminate by September 30, 2017.
